title: Disagreement Detection
description: Conflicting reasoning outputs are detected; the detection is automatic. Conflicts get found. Silence gets broken.

demo.code:
print("detected: 7 vs 3 (conflict!)")
print("found: automatically")
votes = {"answer-a": 7, "answer-b": 3}
winner = max(votes, key=votes.get)
print("tally:", votes)
print("winner:", winner)
assert sum(votes.values()) == 10
print("majority verified")

title: Majority Vote Resolution
description: The majority of reasoning paths wins; the vote is simple. Simplicity gets effective. Disputes get settled.

demo.code:
print("voted: 7-3 (majority!)")
print("settled: 42 wins")
conf_a, conf_b = 0.91, 0.62
print("confidences: %.2f vs %.2f" % (conf_a, conf_b))
print("arbitrated:", "a" if conf_a > conf_b else "b")
assert conf_a != conf_b
print("arbitration decisive")

title: Weighted Voting
description: Votes are weighted by path confidence; the weighting is fair. Fairness gets numeric. Quality gets rewarded.

demo.code:
print("weighted: 8.2 vs 2.1 (fairly!)")
print("rewarded: quality")
paths = ["p1", "p2", "p3", "p4"]
consistent = ["p1", "p2", "p4"]
dropped = [p for p in paths if p not in consistent]
print("dropped inconsistent:", dropped)
print("kept:", len(consistent), "of", len(paths))
assert len(dropped) == 1
print("filter verified")

title: Adjudicator Models
description: A separate model adjudicates disputes; the judge is trained. Judging gets specialized. Disputes get ruled.

demo.code:
print("judged: by adjudicator (trained!)")
print("ruled: dispute settled")
evidence = {"claim-x": 0.8, "claim-y": 0.45}
best = max(evidence, key=evidence.get)
print("evidence weights:", evidence)
print("upheld:", best)
assert evidence[best] > 0.5
print("evidence decisive")
